rationale: Lake Havasu City approved assignment of the specified FBO leases and fueling sublease to Velocity Havasu Holdings, LLC; Velocity then announced its completed acquisition of Havasu's FBO assets as a fourth network location. Current first-party evidence presents the operation as Velocity Lake Havasu within the Tallvine-backed Velocity FBO Network. The transaction expressly excluded seller-retained aircraft management and Northstar maintenance, so Havasu is a child operating location and acquisition lineage rather than a separate manager-level Tallvine company.
proposalGuardrails: Keep Velocity FBO Network as the sole manager-level Tallvine portfolio company and retain Havasu Air Center only as a legacy alias and acquisition lineage.
Preserve Velocity Havasu Holdings, LLC as the local assignee beneath the platform rather than creating another PortCo.
Preserve the September 9, 2025 city approval and October 1, 2025 public completion announcement as distinct milestones.
Treat the legal closing date as not publicly disclosed or closed by October 1, 2025; do not store October 1 as an exact private effective date.
Keep the Sites 3, 4 and 6 FBO leases and Sites 1 and 2 fueling sublease beneath Velocity.
Exclude aircraft-management operations and Northstar Aviation Services maintenance because the sellers retained them.
Do not infer transaction value, Tallvine fund, ownership percentage or the full upstream holdco chain.
Verify that the later Velocity FBO Network task covers the same canonical parent before superseding it.
recommendedNextAction: Prepare one later protected canonical merge and redirect proposal from Havasu Air Center to Velocity FBO Network, preserving city-approval and acquisition lineage and excluding seller-retained businesses.
